dex.entry: A little brass snuffer-cap of a kin that hops from wick to wick at bedtime and sits on each flame until it goes out. In Stillwater a Dousecap on the windowsill means the house has gone to sleep, and nobody minds the dark there.

art.silhouette: A small round kin shaped like a candle-snuffer's bell cap, front three-quarter view: a tarnished-brass cone that is body and hat in one, its tip curling up into a tiny wisp of grey smoke, a soft charcoal-grey face peeping out from under the wide brim with two big sleepy half-closed eyes and a small content smile, and two stubby charcoal feet. A faint warm ember-glow shows under the rim where it last sat on a flame. At 64px it reads as a tiny sleepy brass cap on little legs.
art.palette: Tarnished brass cone (warm ochre-gold with darker umber shading and one pale highlight streak); charcoal-grey face and feet (#2a2633); the eyes deep night (#0b1026) with one bone (#f5f0e1) highlight each; a soft fire-amber (#ff8a3d) ember glow under the rim, the brightest pixel; the smoke-curl pale grey; ink (#1a1430) outlines.
art.direction: Drowsy, dutiful and sweet: a tidy little kin that puts the lights to bed. Cosy-melancholy, round and huggable, never spooky. Must read as the same line as Shutterwick: same brass snuffer-cap, same charcoal, same sleepy eyes.
